panels.rationale: Single human-patient gallbladder histology image showing fibrinoid necrosis of small artery with mural inflammatory infiltrate. Caption plus in-text explicitly attribute findings to polyarteritis nodosa in a gallbladder vasculitis case report. panels.attribution_text: Kitzing et al. Hepatobiliary scintigraphy in vasculitis of the gallbladder as a manifestation of polyarteritis nodosa: a case report.. Cases journal 2009. doi:10.1186/1757-1626-2-9300. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathology of the gallbladder of a 23-year-old white female with a three week history of right upper quadrant pain showing fibrinoid necrosis of a small artery, associated with lymphocytes and macrophages infiltrating the wall. Occasional eosinophils are present. These findings are consistent with gallbladder vasculitis.
in_text_mentions: Macroscopic examination of the gallbladder showed no gross abnormality. However, microscopic examination revealed a striking vasculitis affecting small to medium sized vessels, predominantly arteries. There was fibrinoid necrosis of many vessels associated with an inflammatory cell infiltrate, composed predominantly of lymphocytes with very occasional eosinophils (Figure 4). Almost every vessel in the histological sections was affected and some showed thrombotic occlusion. The findings were consistent with polyarteritis nodosa.
